config.hyperspace_wormholes.title: Hyperspace & Wormholes Settings
config.hyperspace_wormholes.server: On a server, the server's own settings file is used.
config.hyperspace_wormholes.hoopaPity.ti: Determines the total amount of distortions required to enter before you are guaranteed to find Hoopa. 0 turns this off. Example: 6 guarantees Hoopa on the 6th splice in a row without it.
config.hyperspace_wormholes.necrozmaPity: Total White Wormholes for Necrozma Boss

Determines the total amount of white wormholes required to enter before you are guaranteed to find Necrozma. 0 turns this off. Example: 6 guarantees Necrozma on the 6th white wormhole in a row without it.
config.hyperspace_wormholes.hardMode.tip: Hard Mode increases the difficulty of the bosses by raising their levels and increasing their stats. Hard Mode is available after defeating that boss once with this option off. Example: On makes even a first fight against Hoopa a hard one.
config.hyperspace_wormholes.shiny0.tip: The chance a regular Pokémon past a wormhole with no rings is shiny, as 1 in this number. Pokémon from the Item Analyser use it too. 0 means never. Example: 100 is a 1% chance, 50 is 2%.
config.hyperspace_wormholes.shiny1.tip: The chance a regular Pokémon past a wormhole with 1 ring is shiny, as 1 in this number, after flying 5,000 light-years or more. Shorter rides get less, down to the no-ring odds. 0 means never. Example: 10 is a 10% chance, 20 is 5%.
config.hyperspace_wormholes.shiny2.tip: The chance a regular Pokémon past a wormhole with 2 rings is shiny, as 1 in this number, after flying 5,000 light-years or more. Shorter rides get less, down to the no-ring odds. 0 means never. Example: 5 is a 20% chance, 4 is 25%.
config.hyperspace_wormholes.shiny3.tip: The chance a regular Pokémon past a wormhole with 3 rings is shiny, as 1 in this number, after flying 5,000 light-years or more. Shorter rides get less, down to the no-ring odds. 0 means never. Example: 3 is about a 33% chance, 2 is 50%.
config.hyperspace_wormholes.legendaryShi: The chance a legendary, mythical or paradox Pokémon past a wormhole or from the Item Analyser is shiny, as 1 in this number. Necrozma counts too. 0 uses Cobblemon's own shiny rate. Example: 0 with Cobblemon's default is 1 in 8192, 100 is a 1% chance.
config.hyperspace_wormholes.ultraBeastSh: The chance an Ultra Beast past a wormhole or from the Item Analyser is shiny, as 1 in this number. 0 uses Cobblemon's own shiny rate. Example: 0 with Cobblemon's default is 1 in 8192, 100 is a 1% chance.
config.hyperspace_wormholes.griefing.tip: Enable/Disable lightning and Pokémon's moves from destroying Data Monitors. Example: Off keeps every Data Monitor safe, so it never needs crafting back.
Turn each way of getting a legendary on or off, for example if you'd rather get them from Legendary Monuments.
config.hyperspace_wormholes.hyperspaceLe: Whether a legendary can appear on a Hyperspace trip (5-star distortions). Example: Off means no Hyperspace legendaries; Megas and regular Pokémon still come.
config.hyperspace_wormholes.wormholeLege: Whether a legendary can wait past a wormhole in the Ultra Space Wilds. Example: Off means red, green, yellow and blue wormholes always lead to regular Pokémon. Ultra Beasts are not affected.
Whether you can catch Hoopa and Necrozma after beating them. Example: Off means the boss leaves once it's beaten; Hoopa's Prison Bottle still drops.
config.hyperspace_wormholes.cosmogSummon: Whether the Item Analyser can summon Cosmog from a full Jar of Cosmic Energy and a Golden Apple. Cosmog evolves into Solgaleo or Lunala, the mounts for the Ultra Warp Ride. Example: Off means the jar and apple do nothing in the machine.
config.hyperspace_wormholes.monuments.ti: Only matters with Legendary Monuments installed. Monuments: its legendaries are left out of Hyperspace and you get them from its shrines. Both: they can also appear in Hyperspace. Example: Both lets Lugia show up in Hyperspace too.
config.hyperspace_wormholes.maxDistortio: Lets you increase or decrease the amount of distortions around per player. Example: 4 keeps up to 4 around you in busy areas and 2 in quiet ones. 0 to 16.
config.hyperspace_wormholes.distortionMi: How many minutes a distortion stays before it disappears. Example: 30 makes new ones last half an hour. Ones already there keep their time. 1 to 10080.
config.hyperspace_wormholes.distortionsA: On: new distortions don't appear near where online players respawn or in chunks players have spent an hour around. Off: they can appear anywhere.
config.hyperspace_wormholes.distortionBa: How many blocks from online players' respawn points distortions keep when they stay away from bases. Example: 200 keeps them 200 blocks away. 0 to 1000.
config.hyperspace_wormholes.hyperspaceLe: The chance a Hyperspace legendary is shiny, as 1 in this number. Donut shiny boosts multiply it, as they do for regular Pokémon. 0 uses Cobblemon's own shiny rate. Example: 0 with Cobblemon's default is 1 in 8192, 100 is a 1% chance.
config.hyperspace_wormholes.stars.tip: Modify the weight of distortion ratings. Each number is how likely that rating is compared with the others. Example: setting 5 Star to 35 makes 5-star distortions as common as 1-star ones.
config.hyperspace_wormholes.star.tip: How likely a %s Star distortion is compared with the other ratings. 0 means never. Example: with the defaults, 35 out of 100 distortions are 1 Star.
config.hyperspace_wormholes.donuts.tip: How strong each Flavor Power from a donut is. 1 is normal, 2 is twice as strong, 0 turns that power off.
config.hyperspace_wormholes.sparkling.ti: Sparkling Power gives a Hyperspace trip extra shiny rolls. 2 gives twice as many extra rolls. Example: 0 makes Sparkling donuts give no shiny boost.
config.hyperspace_wormholes.alpha.tip: Alpha Power makes Alpha Pokémon more common in Hyperspace. 2 doubles the bonus. Example: 0.5 halves the bonus.
config.hyperspace_wormholes.humungo.tip: Humungo Power makes Pokémon in Hyperspace spawn larger. 2 doubles the size increase. Example: 0 keeps every Pokémon its normal size.
config.hyperspace_wormholes.teensy.tip: Teensy Power makes Pokémon in Hyperspace spawn smaller. 2 doubles the size decrease. Example: 0 keeps every Pokémon its normal size.
config.hyperspace_wormholes.item.tip: Item Power gives Floating Poké Balls a chance to drop Golden Floating Poké Ball loot. 2 doubles that chance. Example: 0.5 halves that chance.
config.hyperspace_wormholes.bigHaul.tip: Big Haul adds extra items to every Floating Poké Ball you pop. 2 doubles the extra items. Example: 0 gives no extra items.
config.hyperspace_wormholes.encounter.ti: Encounter Power raises how many Pokémon stay around you in Hyperspace. 2 doubles the extra Pokémon. Example: 0 gives no extra Pokémon.
config.hyperspace_wormholes.catching.tip: Catching Power gives a failed Poké Ball throw in Hyperspace a chance to catch anyway. 2 doubles that chance. Example: 0 turns the second chance off.
